cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans appreciate the deep engine building, varied deck types, and multiple difficulty stakes, though random elements can cause frustrating late losses.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game features multiple difficulty levels known as stakes, along with different deck types.

citations.review_text: One of my favorite games of all time for a reason. This game is so meticulously well balanced that there is a near infinite number of ways to reach ante 8 and every single joker has its use cases. Sure, Gold Stake drastically decreases the amount of consistently viable ways to win your run, but every hand type can still be the core focus of your build. This game is helplessly addictive, and having every single achievement won't stop me from coming back for more.

Game is good for the first 100 or so hours. It's fun finishing a lot of the achievements with different stakes etc at first but later you just want to achieve high score. Then right around 200+ hours you know each joker by heart and best combos. 
The game desperately needs more jokers and game modes which modders have succeeded in doing with multiplayer. 

I highly recommend it for the price.
i have been going through all the decks and getting gold stake with each. beat black deck gold stake and now im doing nebula. amazing game

The quick learning curve for a rogue lite is important. Using the common knowledge of poker hands and speedy loads time immediately allow for runs to fly by and the difficulty curves of higher stakes and challenges keep you coming back.

The king of deck building roguelikes. 

At first glance, Balatro feels almost entirely RNG. Starting off as any poker game, that’s by design. After a handful of runs, you’ll understand that this game is rooted in rewarding purposeful decision-making. It's here the game begins to open up.

In this game, you build an engine centered around discovering joker combinations and manipulating your deck. Your long term goal is to optimize your hand scoring by improving your deck, jokers, and economy. Each run is unique and the decisions you make in each run feel meaningful. You’ll decide things like if spending money one round is worth losing interest next round on potentially better options in the shop. Or which planet cards to prioritize, down to crafting your deck.

Balatro has varying levels of difficulty in the form of stakes and types of decks, each with different rules and conditions that make the game challenging even after hundreds of hours. Another great benefit as a deckbuilder - it's incredibly easy to put this game down at any given moment. Being able to step away to change a diaper or be Dad was a huge plus for me.

10/10 - Looking forward to what LocalThunk has cooking in the next update. Earning C++ was a blast!

Pros
Endless possible runs
Decision-making at every turn
Rewarding progression

Cons
No more Gold Sticker Jokers left to earn

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay loop as combining random elements with strategic decision-making and engine-building.

citations.review_text: this game isn't comparable to anything, it perfected and popularized roguelike/lite deckbuilders (alongside slay the spire) and there is near infinite replay value. when taking mods into consideration, you can literally play this forever. this game has a combination of RNG being deeply incorporated into the core of the game while also having immense skill expression, which seems hard to pull off, as this game has been copied hundreds of times, nothing comes close. localthunk is absolutely insane. a big downside is that i played this game until i got sick of it and tried to find something comparably good but never found it. i just come back again and again, ♥♥♥♥ you

I love Balatro. The game has the look and feel of a card game but eventually feels like a puzzle, where you are given a random assortment of pieces that you must build into a point-scoring machine. Then, once you have solved the puzzle, it becomes a sandbox where you can experiment with tons of different strategies and styles. The game is challenging at first, but never feels overly punishing. That challenge is what hooked me and kept me playing through the decks and difficulty levels. What I don't like about this game is how addicting it is. It took over most of my free time for a good few months. I only play every now and then these days. I guess 150 hours was enough.

This is a timeless classic that could probably have gone for twice the price and still would have had millions in sales. Streamers have earned a living due to the popularity of simply watching others play.

There is huge variety and replayability here and it can challenge those who are true experts at strategy. Sure, you can leave it up to luck, but you can turn those odds to your favor and make your hand a practical certainty.

This is the standard that others try to emulate. It is a successful game because it truly does it well.

Addictive Relaxation: Balatro is my go-to time waster that lets me either play for short spurts over breakfast or for hours trying to figure out the math and combinations required to beat the harder challenges. 
I somewhat like Solitaire and Texas Hold'em but this immediately hooked me.

Pros:
- Easy to pick up, Difficult to Master. Makes it easy to pick up and put down if you start to feel frustrated.
- 2D Retro Aesthetic, if it works for you, will make Balatro timeless.
- Gamer friendly mindset - no packs to buy and if you don't want to unlock all the cards through gameplay you can select a save that unlocks it all for you.

Cons:
- Like Texas Hold 'Em: Random card pulls or store options can lead to frustration. Great games can be ruined late by this.
- Some runs require patience to avoid mistakes on which cards and modifiers to use.
- You need a reasonably sized screen to get the most out of it (mostly for Portmaster users thinking of putting it on a 4 inch or smaller screen. Steamdeck, etc., should be fine)
